newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Burger King U.S. ad outlay at $300 mln.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Burger King U.S. ad outlay at $300 mln.

text.p: Grand Metropolitan Plc unit Burger King is once again stepping up its U.S. advertising spending by more than 10 percent and expects to spend at least $300 million promoting its hamburgers in the year through September 30.
"Our advertising budget has grown by double digits for the last three years," said Paul Clayton, worldwide marketing chief for Burger King, a unit of Grand Metropolitan.
Clayton also told Reuters the company's U.S. restaurants run by franchisees were also likely to spend an additional $40 million more on marketing and promotion.
Burger King will spend $300 million on U.S. advertising and spending, including tie-ins to next summer's scheduled release of a sequel to the hit film "Jurassic Park."

Promotional spending will also increase in Europe, Clayton said. Outlays there should be about five percent of Burger King's targeted $1 billion of European revenues in the fiscal year through September 30, he said.
